The problem

One AI answer is a first draft.

It sounds sure even when it's wrong, and checking it becomes your job.

?

Confident, not checked

A single model writes and grades its own answer. Nothing independent stands between a mistake and you.

✎

You do the proofreading

Figures, logic and formatting all need checking by hand before anything goes to a client or a board.

⧉

Text, not a deliverable

You still copy it into Word or PowerPoint and fix the layout yourself.

How Wrexlyn fixes it

Draft. Cross-check. Repair. Verify.

The Proprietary Convergence Protocol never lets an engine grade its own work: a different engine reviews every draft, and the final answer is checked against what you asked for.

  1. Draft Each engine works on its part. C1, C2, D1 or free models.
  2. Cross-review A different engine checks every draft for errors and gaps.
  3. Repair Problems go back with specific fixes, up to two rounds.
  4. Verify An independent check against your success criteria, then an honest verdict.
Wrexlyn OS · the algorithms

The algorithms are the product.

Inside Wrexlyn OS, the engine behind coding tasks, bots and automations, every model call runs through a control loop of named, unit-tested algorithms. It isn't a prompting trick, and the model never grades itself.

★
The Proprietary Convergence ProtocolEngages only when a plain repair has already failed: where weaker models usually get stuck.
  1. 1Divergent diagnosisTwo independently framed root-cause guesses from the same evidence, not one.
  2. 2Pairwise adjudicationThe two diagnoses are judged against each other, and a winner is picked with a margin.
  3. 3Lesson-steered regenerationLessons learned from past failures are retrieved and applied at the moment of repair.
  4. 4Convergence scoreThe outcome feeds a fixed, proprietary scoring formula, so confidence reflects what actually happened.
Bots

Teammates that run your work.

Give a bot a name and a one-line role. It works on the engine you choose, runs on a schedule, learns how you like things done, hands work to other bots, and stops for your approval before anything that matters.

Chat & group threadsMessage a bot like a colleague, or put several bots in one thread to coordinate.
RoutinesWeekdays at set times, every few minutes or hours, monthly, when a file lands in a folder, or after another bot finishes.
Teach a taskDescribe the steps once, or point at a past chat. It becomes a reusable skill.
ApprovalsBots stop before sending, publishing, deleting or buying, and wait for you.
DelegationA bot can hand work to other bots and gets their reports back.
Memory & activityYour preferences carry into every run, and every run is logged with its trigger, report and files.
